statement: An international body gains inspection or compute-verification powers covering >= 2 of the top-5 compute jurisdictions (treaty text, official gazettes; by 2029-12-31)
status_at_phase_end: Not met in 2023. Ideas for an IAEA-style agency were floated by a developer and the UN process started, but the main intergovernmental output (a summit declaration signed by both Bloc A and Bloc B) created no body and no inspection or verification powers.

items.summary: A top-5 developer proposed that superintelligence efforts above a capability or compute threshold eventually be subject to an international authority able to inspect systems, require audits and test compliance, modelled on the nuclear agency; a proposal only.
items.detail: OpenAI, 'Governance of superintelligence', 2023-05-22 (Altman, Brockman, Sutskever); proposes 'something like an IAEA' and a possible agreed cap on the rate of frontier capability growth.

items.summary: A summit declaration signed by Bloc A, Bloc B and other states committed signatories to cooperate on frontier-AI risk 'through existing international fora' and future summits; non-binding, created no body and no inspection or verification powers.
items.detail: The Bletchley Declaration by Countries Attending the AI Safety Summit, 1-2 November 2023 (Bloc G GOV.Bloc G). Signatories included the Bloc A and Bloc B (and the Bloc C).

items.summary: A UN high-level advisory body on AI published an interim report on global AI governance; advisory, conferring no inspection or verification powers on any institution.
items.detail: UN Secretary-General's High-level Advisory Body on AI, interim report 'Governing AI for Humanity', December 2023 (landing page confirms December 2023 interim report; exact day approximate). Landing page also refers to the Sept 2024 final report, which is outside the phase and not used here.
